title: Sick Leave in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Tell your employer before your shift starts.** That duty is yours and it is separate from the certificate. The certificate itself is only due once you are off for **more than three calendar days**, unless your contract demands it sooner, and many Berlin contracts do.
**Six weeks of full pay means 42 calendar days, not 42 working days.** It only starts after **four uninterrupted weeks** in the job, and weekends inside a spell are counted.

**The same illness does not get a fresh six weeks.** A new 42 days opens only after **six months free of that illness**, or **twelve months** from the first day you were off with it. The earlier of the two dates wins.

**Krankengeld is 70 percent of gross, capped at 90 percent of net**, and capped again at **135.63 euros a day** in 2026, about **4,069 euros** a month before your own contributions of roughly 12.4 percent. It runs **78 weeks in three years** for one illness, the six weeks included.

**One day of gap ends it.** On Krankengeld the next certificate must be issued at the latest on the **next Werktag** after the last certified day, and Saturdays do not count. Book the follow-up before the current one expires.

**Child sick days shrink on 1 January 2027.** In 2026 it is **15 working days per child per parent**, capped at 35, and 30 for single parents, capped at 70. From 2027 it falls back to **10 and 20**, capped at 25 and 50.

**In Berlin, 116117 is the number that finds you a doctor** round the clock, including the Bereitschaftspraxen that can write a certificate on a Sunday. A doctor may establish incapacity on any calendar day.
